title: Allocator + KV heuristics weekly scrub — Aug 31 - Sep 8 2025
content:
Objective:
Quick weekly scrub focused on allocator heuristics, KV-cache shadowing experiments, and micro-batch slicing changes pushed to canary last Wed. This doc captures what we observed in staging and early prod traffic, open questions, short-term mitigations, and owner-level action items.

Participants:
Marcus (owner), Priya, Liam, Ava, Diego, Kala (observability consult) — async notes collected from the Monday sync and followups.

High-level summary:
- Allocator: new soft-affinity allocator landed in canary (PR 4127). Reduces cross-SMT kernel handoffs but introduced intermittent tail-LAT spikes for >256 token sequences under high concurrency.
- KV cache: shadow cache for prefix reuse rolled for 24h on staging; effective hit rate ~8% overall but 22% on conversational workloads. Shadow evictions clustered around a small set of hot keys.
- Batching: micro-batch-slicing enabled; average tokens/sec improved, but observed batch-splitting race that doubled scheduling latency for ~0.6% of requests.

Telemetry & metrics observed:
- 95th token latency (canary): +7ms on long sequences (baseline 46ms -> 53ms).
- KV shadow hit rate: overall 8% (conversational subset 22%); shadow warmed after 45 minutes of sustained load.
- Eviction churn: 3x higher than expected on hot-key set "session-prefix-*/user-*".
- Batch-slicing anomaly: 0.6% of requests saw scheduling loop requeue, adding median +120ms to end-to-end.
- Cost impact (est): staging shows ~2.1% token-cost reduction realized once hot-key smoothing applied.

Root cause hypotheses:
1) Allocator handshake with the new affinity rules causes kernel context switches when a request crosses a soft-capacity boundary; under long sequences, the KV cache index (and subsequent KV fetch) lands on a different compute slice, introducing cache thrash and tail latency.
2) KV shadowing revealed skewed key popularity; eviction policy (LRU with time windows) isn't prioritizing semantic-session prefixes, so hot keys get evicted during normal churn.
3) Batch-slicing race: concurrent slicer and scheduler both attempt to reassign partial-batches; missing a compare-and-set around the slice-to-worker mapping causes double-scheduling in rare cases.

Experiment notes (what we ran this week):
- Allocator tweak A: softened rebalancing frequency from 50ms -> 150ms on canary. Immediate effect: reduced tail spikes by ~40% in synthetic long-seq runs. Deployed at 09:10 UTC Wed. (owner: Priya)
- KV shadow heatmap: dumped top-5k keys to BigQuery hourly; added smoothing window to eviction scoring (owner: Liam). Observed top 200 keys account for 38% of hits.
- Batch-slicing fix candidate: introduced CAS on slice ownership (branch: fix/slice-cas). Unit tests pass; stress harness showed elimination of double-schedule across 1M simulated requests. (owner: Ava)

Action items (short-term, owners):
- Priya: promote allocator rebalancing change to staging canary policy and run 48h soak. Add metric for "allocator-migrations" to measure cross-worker handoffs. Due: 2025-09-10.
- Liam: adjust KV eviction scoring to include a frequency-weighted TTL component; run shadow re-eval and produce heatmap report. Due: 2025-09-09.
- Ava: land slice-CAS PR, roll to canary with detailed tracing enabled for scheduling path. Correlate any requeue traces back to request ids. Due: 2025-09-11.
- Diego: create synthetic traffic profile that mixes long-seq (>512 tokens) conversational flows and short completions to reproduce canary tail spikes locally. Due: 2025-09-12.
- Marcus: coordinate with Observability (Kala) to add a lightweight span that tags "kv-hot-evicted" and "allocator-migrated" for 2 weeks. Due: 2025-09-09.

Decisions & tradeoffs:
- We will accept a modest increase in average allocator decision latency to reduce migration frequency. Rationale: tail-latency impacts user experience and downstream timeouts more than a ~1-2ms decision delay.
- We will bias eviction to keep session-prefix keys for 10s longer under conversation routes; this is a targeted heuristic, not a global TTL change.

Open questions / risks:
- Does the affinity change interact poorly with multi-tenant scheduling when bursts push across shards? Need a stress test that simulates tenant-local hot keys plus global bursts. (related JIRA INF-2314)
- Hot-key smoothing could increase memory usage by ~6% in worst-case; does Dedicated seat memory reservation cover that? Check with infra cost model.
- Batch-slicing CAS fix reduces race, but adds atomic ops under high throughput — evaluate perf overhead at 99th percentile.

Notes from oncall incidents this week:
- Sep 2: brief degradation on canary during internal load test; root cause traced to allocator rebalancing happening aggressively during a GC spike on one node. Mitigation: pause rebalancing during GC detection window. (temporary patch rolled by Priya)
- Sep 5: KV shadow reported 412k evictions in 1h for a traffic spike; heatmap attributed it to a misbehaving test client that created thousands of unique prefixes. Follow-up: add client-side guardrails to prevent accidental synthetic key explosion. (Diego)

Next week plan (rough):
- Land and roll slice-CAS; monitor scheduling traces for regressions.
- Promote allocator soften to more canary capacity, add migration-counter and tie to rollout gates.
- Finalize KV eviction smoothing and produce a short runbook describing metrics to watch and rollback criteria.
- Run multi-tenant stress test (Diego + Priya) and include Dedicated memory model check (Finance/Infra).

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Relevant PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4127 (allocator), github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4156 (kv-heatmap), github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4179 (slice-cas candidate).
- JIRA: INF-2314 (allocator tail-latency), INF-2341 (kv-eviction-hotkeys).
- Short grep snippet used for heatmap sample: `log.query("kv_fetch", {route: "conv-1", since: -1h}) | top_keys(5000)`

Notes-to-self / informal:
- If the heatmap still shows concentrated hot keys after smoothing, consider introducing a tiny per-key lease so that once a key is promoted it can't be evicted for N seconds. Might be useful for session affinity.
- Remember to add a short blurb to the Friday all-hands about the cost wins from shadow caching (small but noteworthy).

If anything looks off or you have other points observed in canary, add inline comments in this doc and ping Marcus.
